audit.whatIsWrong: Frost Armor's slow immunity is absent from the entire entry, in both layers, while the entry's opening line of advice is 'Tongue Lash's range lets you slow her'.
audit.why: Fury of the North gives Sejuani Frost Armor after she has been out of combat, and Frost Armor grants immunity to slows outright. Tahm Kench opens essentially every exchange against a Sejuani who has been standing in lane — which is to say, against slow immunity. The single ability the entry builds its whole game plan on does not do the thing it is being credited for. This is the reason a 47.03% matchup feels worse than the number: the player is repeatedly told to kite with a slow that is not landing. The stack still applies and the 3-stack stun still works, because a stun is not a slow, so the fix is not despair, it is reframing Tongue Lash as a stack-builder and stun-setup rather than a kiting tool.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor makes her immune to slows, so your Q slow does nothing on her opener — but the An Acquired Taste stack still applies and the 3-stack stun still lands. Chip her from 900 to keep her in combat so Frost Armor never comes back, and only then do your slows work.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers make Permafrost the cooldown to play around: full breakdown.cooldowns says 'Sejuani Permafrost: matchup-defining', breakdown.mid says 'Trade strictly around Permafrost: when it is down, run your full pattern', and dosFull[2] says 'Q-stun at 3 stacks when Permafrost is down'.
audit.why: Permafrost is a 1.5 second cooldown. It is never down. Waiting for it produces a player who never commits. The gate on her stun is Frost stacks, not the timer — Permafrost only fires on a target at maximum Frost, and Frost comes from Winter's Wrath and her attacks. The cooldown genuinely worth tracking is Arctic Assault at 18/16.5/15/13.5/12: it is her only engage, it knocks up, and it stops dead on the first enemy champion it hits.
audit.corrected: Stop tracking Permafrost — it is 1.5 seconds. Track your own Frost stacks and her Arctic Assault, which is 18s at rank 1 and is the only way she closes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (E Permafrost cd 1.5, W Winter's Wrath, Q Arctic Assault cd 18/16.5/15/13.5/12)

audit.whatIsWrong: Frost stacks are consistently called 'Permafrost shards' — 'Sejuani's Permafrost passive activates at 2-3 autos — the shard proc', 'stack Permafrost shards and proc the shard slow', 'Permafrost shard proc gives her a free E stun'.
audit.why: There is no shard. Permafrost is the stun itself; the resource it consumes is Frost, applied by Winter's Wrath and her attacks. Inventing a mechanic name makes the real tell — the Frost debuff counter on your own health bar — invisible to the reader.
audit.corrected: Watch the Frost stacks on yourself; at maximum, Permafrost can stun you at will.

audit.whatIsWrong: Winter's Wrath is credited with 'percent-current-HP damage' in five places (spikes[2], wants.foe[1], mid, whys[2], whys[5]), and the claim carries the entry's whole late-game thesis.
audit.why: Riot's text for Winter's Wrath is 'swings her mace twice, dealing damage, slowing enemies and applying Frost stacks' — no health-scaling component, and the kit file sets no percentHealth flag on it. Meanwhile the burst the entry is trying to describe is real and is in the kit, just on a different ability: Fury of the North lets Sejuani shatter a stunned enemy for massive magic damage. Attributing it to W sends the player dodging the wrong ability. I have replaced the framing where the sentence was primarily about it and left it where I could not do so without speculating.
audit.corrected: Her damage spike is the passive shatter on a stunned target, not Winter's Wrath ticks. Avoid being stunned at all rather than trying to out-heal a W.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (P Fury of the North, W Winter's Wrath)

audit.whatIsWrong: Abyssal Dive is never mentioned; whys[3] instead says 'Without Abyssal Voyage you cannot reposition away from Permafrost autos'.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive is a 1000-1200 range knockup available from level 2, and Frost Armor's slow immunity does nothing against a knockup. It is the one engage in Tahm Kench's kit that Sejuani's defensive passive cannot blunt, and the entry claims he has no repositioning at all.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive knocks up, and Frost Armor does not stop knockups — it is your reliable opener here, not the Q slow.

audit.why: content win[] gives Sejuani every stage from level 2 onward, which matches a 47.03% win rate over 438 games. The full layer disagrees — it rates the matchup EVEN at 6/10 and hands Tahm Kench levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items — but the content chart is the one consistent with the data, so I am flagging the full layer's diff rating rather than the chart.
audit.corrected: full diff 'EVEN' / diffRating '6/10' understates a 47.03% matchup; the content chart is right.

edits.before: At level 1 this lane is genuinely neutral — your Tongue Lash range lets you poke and slow her, but Sejuani's base HP is so high that the damage means nothing, and she is already building Permafrost shards with every auto she lands on you. Step up to last-hit with Q and let Thick Skin start converting her retaliatory autos passively, but respect that her shards can proc into an E stun the moment she reaches two or three autos on you. Your level 2 spike matters less here than in most matchups: the 3-stack stun and Devour combo do work, but pulling her out of lane for three seconds does not hurt a tank who simply walks back at full pressure with percent-HP damage intact.
edits.after: At level 1 your Tongue Lash pokes but does not kite: Sejuani sits on Frost Armor whenever she has been out of combat, and Frost Armor is flat immunity to slows. The stack still applies, so treat Q as a stack-builder here and nothing else. Step up to last-hit and let Thick Skin bank her retaliatory autos, but watch the Frost counter on your own bar — at maximum, Permafrost stuns you whenever she wants, and her passive shatters a stunned target hard. Her Arctic Assault charge is 18 seconds at rank 1 and stops dead on the first champion it touches, so that is the only cooldown here worth counting. Keep her in combat and Frost Armor cannot come back, which is the only way your slow ever matters.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are where this lane genuinely hurts. Without your ultimate you have no repositioning or escape, so Sejuani can freely auto-stack Permafrost and look for an E stun into W spin to dump sustained percent-HP ticks on you — ticks that bypass Thick Skin's grey health because they deal current-HP damage, not flat poke you can idle-heal. When she hits 6, her R changes the calculus entirely: she can cast it reactively the instant you try to commit to a 3-stack Devour, locking you in place and wasting your cooldowns. Play for CS, fish for Tongue Lash pokes from just outside auto range, and activate E pre-emptively to shield incoming burst rather than waiting to heal grey health she will immediately cut through with Winter's Wrath.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are where this lane genuinely hurts. Arctic Assault is her only engage and it is 18 seconds at rank 1, stopping dead on the first champion it touches — that is the one cooldown worth counting, because Permafrost at 1.5 seconds is never down. Once Frost is maxed on you she stuns at will and shatters you with her passive for the burst that actually kills. At 6, Glacial Prison is a 1300-range projectile she can hold for the moment you commit. Play for CS, deny Frost stacks by fighting in short bursts, and press Thick Skin before the stun lands rather than after it. When you do commit, open with Abyssal Dive rather than the Q slow: Frost Armor is immunity to slows and does nothing whatsoever against a knockup.

notes: This is the weakest matchup in my slice at 47.03% over 438 games and it had the worst single defect I found anywhere: the entire game plan rests on Tongue Lash's slow against a champion whose passive grants flat slow immunity. Two cascading consequences — the full layer tells the player to trade around a 1.5-second cooldown, and five separate fields attribute her burst to a percent-HP Winter's Wrath that the kit data does not support. The verified burst is Fury of the North's shatter on a stunned target. I could not verify any health-scaling on Winter's Wrath either way, so I only rewrote the sentences where that claim was the point of the sentence; the phrase may still survive elsewhere in the entry. Also flagged: the full layer rates this matchup EVEN at 6/10, which does not match the win rate — the content level chart is the one that agrees with the data.
